text: On a foggy Saturday morning in July, nineteen forty-five, a B twenty-five bomber, lost in the fog, flew into the Empire State Building. It struck the seventy-ninth floor. Fourteen people were killed. One of its engines plunged into an elevator shaft. Betty Lou Oliver, an elevator operator, was badly hurt. Rescuers put her in an elevator car to take her down. But that elevator's cables had been damaged in the crash. They snapped, and the car fell about seventy-five floors, into the basement.
